column1: Some of the books on criminology actually look pretty interesting, but you've got business to attend to.
column2: 有些犯罪學書籍看起來真的很有趣，但你還有公務要辦。

column1: There are computer manuals, and many interesting books on police work. Hey, what's that copy of "Mad" magazine doing there?
column2: 這裡有電腦手冊，還有許多有趣的警察工作書籍。嘿，那本《Mad》雜誌怎麼會在這裡？

column1: I don't think Lt. Morgan would appreciate your poking around in his things.
column2: 我想 Morgan 中尉不會喜歡你亂翻他的東西。

column1: You wonder what Lt. Morgan keeps in this cabinet. You've heard rumors about Morgan's "liquor cabinet," but you try to ignore the department grapevine. It's usually bull.
column2: 你很好奇 Morgan 中尉在這個櫃子裡放了什麼。你聽過 Morgan 的「酒櫃」傳聞，但試著不理會警局的小道消息。通常都是胡扯。

column1: Don't get fingerprints on the veneer, Bonds.
column2: 別在木皮上留下指紋，Bonds。

column1: Lt. Morgan has pretty nice furniture, though up close, you can see it's nearly as chintzy as most of the other furniture in the building.
column2: Morgan 中尉的家具相當漂亮，不過近看就會發現，和大樓裡其他家具一樣，其實很廉價。

column1: The plant's leaves are soft and green. Somehow, you can't picture Lt. Morgan watering the plants and talking to them.
column2: 植物的葉子柔軟翠綠。不知怎地，你無法想像 Morgan 中尉替植物澆水、對它們說話的模樣。

column1: Uhh, Bonds...just leave that where it is. I don't want the glass smudged. I'd, uh...I'd like to get back to work here, if there's nothing else I can do for you.
column2: 呃，Bonds……就把那放在原位。我不想讓玻璃沾上污痕。我，呃……如果沒別的事，我想回去工作了。

column1: Bonds! Leave that alone. If there's nothing else you wanted, I really should get back to work.
column2: Bonds！別碰那個。如果你沒有其他事，我真的該回去工作了。

column1: A Bachelor of Science in Psychology from Cloun College in Baraboo, Wisconsin.
column2: 威斯康辛州 Baraboo 的 Cloun 學院心理學理學士學位。

column1: Sonny! I'd prefer it if you'd leave that just where it is. Now, I've got a very busy schedule to get to, so I'll have to ask you to skedaddle.
column2: Sonny！我希望你把那留在原位。現在我的行程非常忙，只好請你趕快離開。

column1: A testimonial in consideration of Lt. Morgan's kindness.
column2: 一張表揚 Morgan 中尉善行的獎狀。

column1: Pardon me, Sonny? That's hanging just where I want it. 'Kay? Thanks. Now then, I've got a pile of work here to do, so if you'll excuse me...?
column2: 不好意思，Sonny？那就掛在我想要的位置。好嗎？謝謝。那麼，我還有一堆工作要做，請你先失陪……？

column1: An honorary Doctor of Thinkology degree from the Universitatus Committeeatum e pluribus unum.
column2: Universitatus Committeeatum e pluribus unum 頒發的榮譽 Thinkology 博士學位。

column1: Sonny, I...uh...the cleaning people get very upset if you smear the glass. Besides, we've both got work to do, don't we? So let's get to it!
column2: Sonny，我……呃……如果你把玻璃弄髒，清潔人員會很不高興。再說，我們都有工作要做，不是嗎？那就開始吧！

column1: Now now, Sonny, that's arranged just so, let's not go disturbing it. Now, to work then, shall we? Atta boy.
column2: 好了好了，Sonny，那是特別這樣安排的，別去弄亂它。現在，去工作吧，好嗎？這才乖。

column1: Yes, Bonds, read what that medal says: "Courage." Ain't it the truth? Now, if it's all the same to you, I've got some work to do, so...
column2: 沒錯，Bonds，讀讀那枚勳章寫了什麼：「勇氣」。說得不錯吧？現在，如果你不介意，我還有工作要做，所以……

column1: It's an expensive hardwood hat rack.
column2: 這是昂貴的硬木帽架。

column1: Lt. Morgan probably wouldn't appreciate your fingering his knick-knacks.
column2: Morgan 中尉大概不會喜歡你摸他的擺飾。

column1: It's a Triple Cross for meritorious conduct, extraordinary valor, and conspicuous bravery.
column2: 這是三重十字勳章，表彰功勳行為、非凡勇氣與顯著英勇。

column1: The Lieutenant wouldn't be amused if you pulled his chair out from under him, Bonds.
column2: 如果你把椅子從中尉身下抽走，他可不會覺得好笑，Bonds。

column1: Chairs for Lt. Morgan's guests. Very stylish, you think, remembering your patched and faded 1960's barkalounger.
column2: Morgan 中尉給客人坐的椅子。你覺得很時髦，想起自己那張補丁斑斑、褪色的 1960 年代躺椅。

column1: Don't fiddle with the Lieutenant's stuff. He'll think you're nervous. You are, of course, but you don't want HIM to know that.
column2: 別亂動中尉的東西。他會以為你很緊張。你當然緊張，但不想讓「他」知道。

column1: It's Lt. Morgan's desk lamp.
column2: 這是 Morgan 中尉的桌燈。

column1: It would be presumptuous to use Lt. Morgan's phone.
column2: 擅自使用 Morgan 中尉的電話未免太冒昧。

column1: Lt. Morgan's phone.
column2: Morgan 中尉的電話。

column1: You notice the number is 555-3784.
column2: 你注意到號碼是 555-3784。

column1: Don't touch the plant. It's temperamental.
column2: 別碰那株植物。它脾氣很古怪。

column1: It's a big, happy houseplant.
column2: 這是一株巨大又生氣蓬勃的室內植物。

column1: Talking to plants is good for them, but it makes your superiors think you're nuts.
column2: 和植物說話對它們有益，但會讓長官以為你瘋了。

column1: Lt. Morgan is on the phone and can't be bothered. Shouldn't you be somewhere, Bonds?
column2: Morgan 中尉正在講電話，沒空理你。Bonds，你是不是該去別的地方？

column1: Hmm, nice upholstery. Not like the vinyl guest chairs you've got at home.
column2: 嗯，坐墊很漂亮。不像你家裡那些乙烯基客椅。
